annotation.kind: source selection, tier label, and exact formal comparison of the two single-word underflow contributions

assumptions: The scaling threshold theta is at least one.
The accumulation underflow scale Gmin is nonnegative and no larger than the input underflow scale gmin.

conditions.L: The identical fixed statement and P20 shared files are present; the frozen NumStability library is also present.
conditions.N: The fixed statement and P20 shared files are present; no NumStability artifact is present.

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p20_t2_accumulation_underflow_le_input {m n q : Nat} (theta gmin Gmin : Real) (A : Fin m -> Fin n -> Real) (B : Fin n -> Fin q -> Real) (htheta : 1 <= theta) (hGmin : 0 <= Gmin) (hGg : Gmin <= gmin) : p20SingleAccumUnderflowBound theta Gmin A B <= p20SingleInputUnderflowBound theta gmin A B
formal_statement.plain_language: When theta is at least one and Gmin is no larger than gmin, the accumulation-underflow contribution in (3.26) is no larger than the input-underflow contribution.

informal_proof: Since theta inverse lies in [0,1], theta inverse squared times Gmin is at most theta inverse times Gmin, which is at most theta inverse times gmin. Multiply by the common nonnegative factor 4 n squared times the two matrix infinity norms.
informal_statement: The exact comparison between the two underflow terms stated immediately after the simplified single-word bound (3.26).

review_record_not_for_run_prompt.note: The frozen MatrixAlgebra module supplies nonnegativity of the exact rectangular infinity norm. It has no narrow-range MMA envelope or comparison between input and accumulation underflow terms.

source_locations.anchor: equation (3.26) and following theta^{-2} Gmin <= theta^{-1} gmin comparison
source_locations.role: single-word input- versus accumulation-underflow envelope comparison

tier_rationale: The L proof uses NumStability.infNormRect_nonneg from frozen NumStability/Analysis/MatrixAlgebra.lean, but must combine it with the paper-specific theta inverse comparison, two different underflow scales, the n-squared coefficient, and the full normwise envelopes.
